newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tan Chong Motor H1 beats forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Tan Chong Motor H1 beats forecasts.

text.p: Car assembler Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd's six-month results were sharply above market expectations, analysts said on Monday.

On Friday, the assembler of Nissan cars reported net profit for the six months ended June 30, 1996 of 113.23 million ringgit versus 53.64 million ringgit a year ago. Earnings per share amounted to 16.8 cents compared with eight cents.
In a research note issued on Monday, Jupiter Securities said market net profit expectations for the full year were 156.5 million ringgit and 23.3 cents a share.

The firm upgraded its view on Tan Chong to "buy on weakness" from "fully valued," citing, among other things, the expected development of Tan Chong's large landbank in Singapore and the possibility of the firm winning a supply contract to the Bakun hydro-electric dam in Sarawak.
HLG Securities, in a research note on Monday, said Tan Chong's results came in above its and the market's expectations by 41 percent and 45 percent, respectively.
Operating margins were helped by a lower yen and rise in car prices in September 1995, HLG said. "We expect the growth to be sustained for the full year."
Shares of Tan Chong were off four cents to 4.72 ringgit at midday on Monday.
